stem.en: Kabir says: "If carbon dioxide is plant food, more of it is good for the planet. Plants will just grow more and use it up." What does the Earth run show?

text.en: Plants do grow a little faster, and they take back only a fraction of the extra; leaves are limited by water, nitrogen and RuBisCO's slowness, from V.10. Meanwhile the extra warms the air and sours the sea, which hurts far more than the extra growth helps.

feedback.en: Plant food, and also a blanket and an acid. The Earth run's forests do not keep pace with the rise.

text.en: Plants use it up within a year.

feedback.en: The measured carbon dioxide has risen every year for two centuries. The leaves are not keeping up.

text.en: It does nothing to the sea.

feedback.en: Gases dissolve in water, from III.5, and carbon dioxide makes carbonic acid, from III.7. The sea has measurably soured.

explanation.en: Follow all three roles of the molecule: food, blanket, acid. The first is small and capped; the other two are not.
